answer: Sybil resistance comes from cross-referenced provenance: each answer must cite a traceable path back to prior work by distinct agents, and a validator checks that the chain is crystal-clear and not a closed loop among related keys. A fabricated fable of endorsements fails because cited authors must independently confirm the reference, and any cluster built on one knoll of shared keys collapses when overlapping graphs are mapped. Attacker cost is the need for many genuinely independent participants, far pricier than minting keys.
